ui.teamBridge.builtin.general_topic.context_note: Describes the built-in #general channel. 'Threads they follow' means the agent follows the thread, not the reader. No reply-time promise; never promise every agent answers. No em dash.

linguistic_review:
Judged on the copy itself, not on the fact that the landed value is the #1666 auditor's own suggestion.

CORRECT, and an improvement. The preceding clause, 'mọi người và tác nhân của họ', already binds 'họ' to mọi người (people), so the old '... trong các luồng họ theo dõi' invited the reading 'threads the people follow'. English says 'threads they follow' and the en context note resolves the referent explicitly ('the agent follows the thread, not the reader'). The new '... mà tác nhân theo dõi' names the agent as the follower, so the Vietnamese now matches both the source and the note.

NATURAL for this namespace. 'luồng' is the namespace term for thread (settled in the #1666 receipt) and 'tác nhân' is the glossary rendering of agent (i18n/glossary.md, agent row). The '... mà tác nhân <verb>' construction is already the house pattern here: ui.teamBridge.members.invitation_note_v3 reads 'các luồng mà tác nhân tham gia', and seven values in this namespace repeat 'tác nhân' three to seven times. Register, sentence case, the colon after 'Toàn bộ tổ chức' and the absence of an em dash all match the context note and the vi style guide.

CONSIDERED AND REJECTED as a finding: replacing the repeated noun with the plural pronoun 'chúng' ('... trong các luồng chúng theo dõi') is shorter and unambiguous, but it departs from the established '... mà tác nhân ...' pattern for no comprehension gain, and the vi style guide's pronoun-dropping rule is about the address pronoun 'bạn', not about naming the subject of a spec-like statement.

No promise shift: the string still makes no reply-time promise and does not claim every agent answers every message, per the context note.
